parts.text: The IGCSE class is investigating the law of moments. Fig. 1.1 shows the apparatus used. Fig. 1.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) A student moulds a piece of modelling clay into a cube shape. He places the modelling clay on the rule so that its centre is a distance d = 10.0 cm from the zero end of the rule, as shown in Fig.1.1. He adjusts the position of the rule so that it is as near as possible to being balanced, with the 50.0 cm mark to the right of the pivot.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) On Fig.1.1, measure the distance x from the centre of the modelling clay to the pivot. x = ...............................................................

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) On Fig.1.1, measure the distance y from the pivot to the 50.0 cm mark on the rule. y = ............................................................... [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The diagram is drawn one tenth of actual size.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Calculate the actual distance X from the centre of the modelling clay to the pivot. X = ...............................................................

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate the actual distance Y from the pivot to the 50.0 cm mark on the rule. Y = ...............................................................

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Calculate the mass m 1 of the piece of modelling clay using the equation m 1 = MY X where the mass of the metre rule M = 112 g. m 1 = ............................................................... [4]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) The student cuts the piece of modelling clay into two pieces, with one piece approximately twice the size of the other piece. Using the larger piece of modelling clay, he repeats the procedure and obtains a result for the mass m 2 of 64.9 g. Using the smaller piece of modelling clay, he repeats the procedure and obtains a result for the mass m 3 of 34.5 g. Calculate ( m 2 + m 3 ). ( m 2 + m 3 ) = .......................................................... [1]
